title: Pawleys Island Gray Man: The ghost that warns of hurricanes
excerpt: South Carolina's Gray Man legend says a ghost warns Pawleys Island of hurricanes and spares homes. Here's what really protects a house from surge and wind.
content:
Gray Man: South Carolina’s ghost said to warn of hurricanes

You're walking along a quiet South Carolina beach as a hurricane barrels toward the coast. The sky is darkening, the wind is picking up, and suddenly, you spot a mysterious figure dressed in gray.

You blink. He's gone.

According to a chilling Lowcountry legend, that could be the Gray Man, a ghostly figure said to appear on Pawleys Island just before a major hurricane strikes.

Even more interestingly, those who claim to have seen him say their homes were spared from the storm.

The story reportedly dates back to 1822, when a young man traveling to visit his love drowned in the area's treacherous marshland.

Local historian Christine Vernon says his fiancée was heartbroken. While walking along the beach and praying for him to return, she suddenly saw a figure approaching from the surf.

"He stops her cold and he points inland and says, 'You and the family are in grave danger. You must leave. A hurricane is approaching,'" Vernon recalled.

The young woman and her family left the island. A few days later, the Great Hurricane of 1822 struck the coast.

Over time, stories emerged of a silent apparition wandering the shoreline ahead of dangerous weather, seemingly warning residents to get out of harm's way.

(MORE: Mystery weather notes found in 1880s dress pocket)

Before Hurricane Hugo devastated parts of South Carolina in 1989, Pawleys Island residents Jim and Clara Moore reported seeing the mysterious figure.

"They saw the gray man and he approached and just pointed inland and told them a storm was coming," Vernon said.

The couple evacuated. When they returned, the destruction was immense.

"Every home to the left, right, and behind their house had been completely not just destroyed, but washed away," Vernon said. "But their house was still standing."

More recent sightings of the Gray Man have been associated with Hurricane Florence in 2018 and Hurricane Ian in 2022.

(MORE: Try these weather-inspired Halloween costumes)

The real forces at work

The Gray Man may belong to folklore, but the forces that determine whether a home survives a hurricane are very real.

Elevation can make a critical difference when storm surge pushes seawater inland. A home's construction also matters: strong roof design, fortified walls, impact-resistant windows and doors and a foundation protected from flooding can make all the difference difference.

And remember, no ghostly sighting is a substitute for evacuation orders or official weather warnings.

The legend endures

So why has this mysterious figure remained part of Pawleys Island's history for more than 200 years?

"I believe because people have hope," Vernon said. "I think they want to believe in something spiritual that will come and actually protect us."

(MORE: How a red sky can tell you if there’s bad weather ahead)

After more than two decades living in the area and authoring The Legend of the Gray Man of Pawleys Island, Vernon believes the Gray Man’s message is this:

"Because he had lost his loved one, his fiance, he would say to hold them dear to you, take good care of them," she said. "And if you have a warning or a gut feeling that something is wrong, listen to that voice, whether it's inside your head or that feeling you have. If you think it's time to leave, protect your family and please leave the area if there's a terrible storm."
